summary: Interpolate scalar fields onto supplied grids or generated ij-indexed grids

capability: Interpolate scalar fields from scattered planar samples onto supplied or generated ij-indexed regular grids.
operation: scattered planar fields to regular-grid samples
scattered xx,yy and matching fields plus optional target grids -> generated or supplied grid coordinates and interpolated fields
discovery.model: SciPy scattered-data interpolation with method=linear by default and default nx=ny=200 when target grids are generated.
discovery.geometry: Planar scattered samples and a generated regular grid; generated output axes use ij order and supplied xi,yi jointly override them.
discovery.boundary: Queries beyond the convex support are excluded and no outside-hull values are synthesized; no nonlinear interpolation accuracy claim is made.

identity.direction: Declared inputs to Tuple xi,yi and interpolated scalar fields
identity.definition: Interpolate scalar fields onto supplied grids or generated ij-indexed grids
identity.model: SciPy scattered-data interpolation; default method=linear and nx=ny=200
identity.geometry: planar scattered samples and generated regular grid
identity.coordinates: xx,yy generic planar coordinates; generated output axes use ij order
identity.boundary: Explicit xi,yi are used together; if either is omitted, both supplied grid axes are replaced
assumptions: Finite matched planar sample arrays and positional field arrays
Requested grid/query points lie inside convex/interpolation support
Fields are passed as separate positional arguments; no values mapping alias is accepted

inputs.name: nx
inputs.description: Number of generated x grid points
inputs.constraints: Integer accepted by numpy.linspace; used when xi or yi is missing

inputs.name: ny
inputs.description: Number of generated y grid points
inputs.constraints: Integer accepted by numpy.linspace; used when xi or yi is missing

inputs.name: xi
inputs.constraints: Used with yi only when both are supplied; if either is None, both axes are generated

inputs.name: yi
inputs.shape: same shape as xi or None
inputs.constraints: Used with xi only when both are supplied; if either is None, both axes are generated

outputs.name: grid_and_fields
outputs.description: Tuple xi,yi and interpolated scalar fields
outputs.shape: tuple of (nx,ny) arrays or supplied grid shape

preconditions: Finite matched planar sample arrays and positional field arrays
Requested grid/query points lie inside convex/interpolation support
Fields are passed as separate positional arguments; no values mapping alias is accepted
supported: Finite inputs satisfying the callable-specific shape, support, and boundary conditions
excluded: No outside-hull value synthesis or nonlinear interpolation accuracy claim

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises TypeError when required arguments are missing, the removed values mapping keyword is used, or an unknown keyword is supplied; raises ValueError when method is outside its documented set or the samples, fields, or query coordinates violate the SciPy interpolation contract; no input repair is inferred.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

python.signature: regular_grid(xx, yy, *fields, nx=200, ny=200, xi=None, yi=None, method='linear')

example.description: Interpolate one positional scattered scalar field onto a generated 4-by-5 regular grid.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.sampling import regular_grid

x, y = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.5, 1.0], [0.0, 0.5, 1.0])
result = regular_grid(x, y, x + y, nx=4, ny=5)
assert len(result) == 3
assert result[2].shape == (4, 5)
example.expected: The return tuple has three entries and the interpolated field has shape (4, 5).
